newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Amicable to seek full bids from suitors.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Amicable to seek full bids from suitors.

text.p: British mutual insurer Scottish Amicable said on Tuesday that after considering a number of bid approaches that had recently been made for the company, it had decided to seek formal offers from all interested suitors.

In a letter to policyholders circulated to the news media, Scottish Amicable said that as well as offers from bank Abbey National Plc and insurer Prudential Corp Plc it had also had "expressions of interest" from others.
"Your board has therefore decided that the right way to achieve the best result for our policyholders is to seek definitive offers from those institutions interested," it said.

The mutual said it would take independent professional advice during the selection process, adding its objective was to maximise financial benefits for with-profits policy holders "taking into account both short-term and long-term returns".
Last month the company sparked takeover interest when it announced it was planning to demutualise and seek a float on the stock exchange.

Abbey National made an initial bid worth about 1.4 billion pounds ($2.29 billion) which was followed by a 1.9 billion pound offer from Prudential a few days later. Analysts have identified other potential bidders as financial services group Halifax Building Society and banking group National Westminster.
Possible international suitors named by market sources include Australian Mutual Provident and Dutch insurance and banking groups Aegon, ING and Fortis Amev NV. ($1=.6120 Pound)
